findings.name: Renaming a model also changes its pin position (and on the first rename rewrites its table visualization settings)
findings.summary: Every rename also changes the model's stored pin position and, on the first rename, its table visualization settings. The app's own History panel says so ('... and changed pin position', first rename: 'changed the visualization settings ... edited the metadata and changed pin position'), and the revision records confirm it: collection_position went 1 → 3 → 9 (the model is re-ordered in Our analytics, agent15-name-B now sorts after the other models) and visualization_settings went from null to {\"table.pivot_column\":\"SOURCE\",\"table.cell_column\":\"LONGITUDE\"}, a highlighted-column setting nobody chose. Seen on both renames I made. (on /model/42-agent15-state-model (model detail header title))
findings.expected: Renaming a model changes its name only: the History entry records the rename and nothing else, and the model's pin position and visualization settings stay exactly as the person left them.
findings.actual: Every rename also changes the model's stored pin position and, on the first rename, its table visualization settings. The app's own History panel says so ('... and changed pin position', first rename: 'changed the visualization settings ... edited the metadata and changed pin position'), and the revision records confirm it: collection_position went 1 → 3 → 9 (the model is re-ordered in Our analytics, agent15-name-B now sorts after the other models) and visualization_settings went from null to {\"table.pivot_column\":\"SOURCE\",\"table.cell_column\":\"LONGITUDE\"}, a highlighted-column setting nobody chose. Seen on both renames I made.
reproSteps: Sign in with eval@momentic.ai / momentic-eval-1 and create (or open) a model whose only edit is a rename — here the model 42 based on Sample Database > People, opened at /model/42-agent15-state-model.
Click the model title at the top left (the field showing 'agent15-state-model'), replace the text with 'agent15-name-A' and press Enter.

Click the info (i) button next to Bookmark and open the History tab: the entry reads 'changed the visualization settings, renamed it from "agent15-state-model" to "agent15-name-A", edited the metadata and changed pin position.'

Rename the same model again, from 'agent15-name-A' to 'agent15-name-B', press Enter, and read the new History entry: 'renamed this Card from "agent15-name-A" to "agent15-name-B" and changed pin position.'
For the stored record of both renames open /api/revision?entity=card&id=42 in the same browser.

findings.name: Metric results include quarters/months far past the metric's own filter, with empty values (and 0s on Number of Orders)
findings.summary: The result contains periods beyond the filter's end: Revenue returns 17 rows (chart x-axis to Q1 2029) with 10 empty future quarters, and Number of Orders returns 49 rows with a line that falls to 0 in January 2027 and stays at 0 through January 2029, i.e. the charts/row counts contradict the filter shown in Edit metric definition. (on /metric/9-revenue (same on /metric/19-number-of-orders))
findings.expected: Only periods that the metric's own filter covers are returned: 7 quarters (Q2 2025 to Q4 2026) for Revenue and months up to the current year for Number of Orders; the chart's x-axis ends at the last in-range period.
findings.actual: The result contains periods beyond the filter's end: Revenue returns 17 rows (chart x-axis to Q1 2029) with 10 empty future quarters, and Number of Orders returns 49 rows with a line that falls to 0 in January 2027 and stays at 0 through January 2029, i.e. the charts/row counts contradict the filter shown in Edit metric definition.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval@momentic.ai / momentic-eval-1 and open Browse > Metrics.
Open the metric "Revenue" in the Examples collection (/metric/9-revenue).
Read the footer: "Showing 17 rows"; the chart x-axis is labelled up to Q1 2029.
Click the small table icon (Switch to data) next to "Visualization" at the bottom of the page.
Read the table: Sum of Total has values only for Q2 2025 to Q4 2026 (3,391.41 ... 67,863.4); rows Q1 2027, Q2 2027, Q3 2027, Q4 2027, Q1 2028 ... Q2 2029 have an empty Sum of Total.
Open "Move, trash, and more…" > "Edit metric definition": the filter is "Created At is in the previous 12 quarters or this quarter" (today is 23 Nov 2026, so nothing after Q4 2026 is in range).

Repeat on Browse > Metrics > "Number of Orders" (/metric/19-number-of-orders): footer says "Showing 49 rows" and the count line drops to 0 from about January 2027 and stays at 0 across January 2028 and January 2029. Its filter is "Created At is in the previous 3 years or this year".

findings.name: Turning the metric \"Number of Orders\" into a model silently applies a \"previous 3 years or this year\" filter and drops 28 months of data

(on /metric/19-number-of-orders (now /model/19-number-of-orders, turned back into the saved question /question/19-number-of-orders))
findings.expected: The converted model/question keeps the metric's own time setting (\"All time\") and returns the same 49 monthly rows with the same counts as the metric did.
findings.actual: Right after \"Turn into a model\" the same card shows only 21 rows (April 2025 → December 2026) and the footer \"Showing 21 rows\"; the months from 2027 to 2029 with counts around 500 each are gone. Turning it back to a saved question leaves a filter chip \"Created At is in the previous 3 years or this year\" and \"View: Previous 3 years or this year\", which the metric never had (its View was \"All time\"). Setting View to \"All time\" and pressing Apply in the date popover brings back \"Showing 49 rows\" and the full chart, so the conversion itself changed the data scope and hides 28 months of data.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval@momentic.ai and open Browse > Metrics > "Number of Orders" (https://5501-ioic2igikzl9eu83lv3wv.e2b.app/metric/19-number-of-orders). Note the footer says "Showing 49 rows", the line chart runs to January 2029 and the View selector says "All time".
Open the "..." menu in the header and click "Turn into a model".

Look at the model that appears: its table has only 21 rows (April 2025 to December 2026) and the footer says "Showing 21 rows" — nothing after December 2026, although the metric showed monthly counts of about 500 for 2027-2029.
